fixes.explanation: True, baker. The LORD says, “Has not My hand made all these things? And so they came into being…” (Isaiah 66:2). I make cookies one stamp at a time and my mustache gets tired. He made everything, and the question shows it. It comes right after He asks what kind of house you could build for Him.

That's it, baker. The LORD says, “This is the one I will esteem: he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word.” (Isaiah 66:2). Notice He doesn't say the one with the biggest anything. I think that's good news for all of us.

Close, but no cookie. The text doesn't say the LORD esteems a famous name. He says He will esteem “he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word.” (Isaiah 66:2). That's the one He points to, and fame isn't part of that description.

Right, baker. The LORD says, “Indeed, they have chosen their own ways and delighted in their abominations.” (Isaiah 66:3). The offerings are right there in the verse, and the LORD still talks about the ways they chose. The verse looks past what they brought to the ways they chose.
Yes, baker. The LORD says, “So I will choose their punishment and I will bring terror upon them…” (Isaiah 66:4). They chose their ways, and now He chooses their punishment. This is a heavy verse.

That's the one, baker. The LORD says, “…because I called and no one answered, I spoke and no one listened.” (Isaiah 66:4). The reason He gives is a call that got no answer. Then He adds what they did instead: “But they did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight.”

Not in this verse, friend. After the brothers say, “Let the LORD be glorified that we may see your joy!” the LORD says, “But they will be put to shame.” (Isaiah 66:5). That is what He says will happen to them. Being proven right isn't what the verse says.

Watchmen are a good guess, but the text names someone else, friend. It says, “It is the voice of the LORD, repaying His enemies what they deserve!” (Isaiah 66:6). The voice from the temple is the LORD's. No watchman is mentioned in the verse.

Not quite, friend. The LORD asks, “Who has heard of such as this? Who has seen such things?” (Isaiah 66:8). Those questions show how astonishing this birth is. It isn't pictured as something people hear about all the time.

Right, baker. He asks, “Who has heard of such as this? Who has seen such things?” (Isaiah 66:8). The questions show how astonishing this is, not something people hear about all the time. If I told you my cookies baked themselves before the oven warmed up, you'd ask the same thing.
Nineveh isn't in this passage, baker. The LORD names the mother in the same verse: “Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children.” (Isaiah 66:8). It's Zion.

Yes, baker. The LORD asks, “Shall I bring a baby to the point of birth and not deliver it?” and then, “Or will I who deliver close the womb?” (Isaiah 66:9). Asked that way, the answer is no, He will not leave the birth undone. In this picture, He delivers.

True, baker. The LORD says, “As a mother comforts her son, so will I comfort you, and you will be consoled over Jerusalem.” (Isaiah 66:13). Think of how a mother's comfort feels. He says that's how He will comfort them. It's a tender verse.
Yes, baker. The verse says, “When you see, you will rejoice, and you will flourish like grass…” (Isaiah 66:14). Not a tall tree, just grass. I think grass is a nice everyday picture.

A cedar sounds grand, friend, but it isn't in this verse. The text says, “When you see, you will rejoice, and you will flourish like grass…” (Isaiah 66:14). The comparison in the verse is grass, not a cedar.

No olive trees in this verse, baker. The text says, “When you see, you will rejoice, and you will flourish like grass…” (Isaiah 66:14). Grass is the comparison the verse uses. It's a simple one, and it fits.
